target.title: [codex] acknowledge terminal Gmail OAuth watch failures
target.body:
## Summary

- classify expired or revoked Gmail OAuth credentials as terminal processing failures
- acknowledge terminal OAuth failures in both Pub/Sub push and pull consumers
- preserve the last successfully processed Gmail history cursor for later catch-up
- keep transient Gmail API, rate-limit, and downstream hook failures retryable

## Root cause

The Gmail watch consumers treated every non-rate-limit processing failure as retryable. When the OAuth refresh token returned `invalid_grant`, push delivery responded with HTTP 500 and pull delivery nacked the message. Pub/Sub then redelivered a failure that cannot recover without operator re-authentication, producing an unbounded retry and log storm.

## User impact

Expired or revoked Gmail credentials now produce a clear re-authentication warning and acknowledge the current Pub/Sub notification without advancing the stored history cursor. A later notification after re-authentication can resume from the last successfully processed history ID. Temporary API failures and hook delivery failures retain their existing retry behavior.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/gmailwatch -run 'Test(HTTPHandlerAcknowledgesTerminalAuthFailure|ProcessorClassifiesTerminalAuthWithoutAdvancingHistory)$'`
- `go test ./internal/cmd -run 'Test(IsTerminalGmailAuthError|GmailWatchPullMessage_AcksTerminalAuthAndPreservesProgress|GmailWatchServer_AcknowledgesTerminalAuthAndPreservesProgress)$'`
- `make fmt-check`
- `make lint`
- `make deadcode`
- `make build`

The broader `internal/cmd` Gmail-watch test selection still has pre-existing shared-state failures when run as one package on this machine. The same failures reproduce on unmodified `upstream/main`; the focused regression tests above pass.

Related OpenClaw lifecycle fix: openclaw/openclaw#96202.
